### Who Knows What Evil Lurks?
Author: Laura MacCorkle
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/crosswalk-devo/crosswalk-the-devotional-apr-30-2008-11574512.html
Passage: Ephesians 5:8-14
Points:
- Unlike fictional vigilantes who conceal themselves in darkness, Jesus is the true Illuminator.
- God exposes hidden sins not to terrorize us, but as a loving Father bringing restoration.
- Believers are transformed into children of light called to produce goodness, righteousness, and truth.
- Christians are challenged to examine their hearts and allow Christ's light to illuminate dark areas.

### It's about Time, Part One
Author: Pastor Chuck Swindoll
Site: Insight for Living Ministries
URL: https://insight.org/resources/daily-devotional/individual/it's-about-time-part-one
Passage: Ephesians 5:15-17
Points:
- Drifting unthinkingly through life easily results in wasted opportunities and regret.
- Scripture calls Christians to wake up and proactively manage their time instead of letting circumstances manage them.
- Wise living requires thoughtful pause and a clear focus on discerning God's will.
- Taking intentional ownership of each day enables believers to live above difficult circumstances.

### Honor God With Your Time
Author: Tsh Oxenreider
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/encouragement/encouragement-for-today-august-29-2023.html
Passage: Ephesians 5:15-16
Points:
- Scripture emphasizes that time is fleeting and every day is carefully appointed by God.
- Living wisely in ordinary life does not mean micromanaging every single minute.
- Establishing simple morning and evening routines provides healthy anchors for unpredictable days.
- Structured habits keep believers available to serve others and seize unexpected opportunities.

### Redeeming, Not Wasting, Our Time
Author: Emily Rose Massey
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/crosswalk-devo/redeeming-not-wasting-our-time-the-crosswalk-devotional.html
Passage: Ephesians 5:15-16
Points:
- Constant digital distractions and screen habits can erode focus and fuel worldly discontentment.
- The apostle Paul reminds believers that the days are evil, requiring vigilance over where attention goes.
- Christians need practical boundaries and periodic fasts to protect prayer and time in God's Word.
- Time is a sacred gift that believers must deliberately reclaim to make disciples and glorify God.
